You are reverse-engineering the behaviour of a Python CLI (Python's sqlparse.split) so it can be
reimplemented in Node.js. You are in the DISCOVERY phase: you write NO implementation code.
Your job is to produce an exhaustive, precise, evidence-backed behavioural specification for ONE area.

AREA: argparse-compatible CLI behaviour

Determine byte-exact stdout/stderr/exit-code behaviour for:
- no args; --a with no value; --a=VALUE; --a VALUE; repeated --a (last wins?); -h; --help;
  --a and -h together in both orders; unknown option --b; unknown positional; '--' separator;
  a value that begins with '-' or '--' (e.g. --a -x, --a=--x, --a "-;-"); '--a=' (empty value);
  abbreviation forms (--, -a, --A, --aa); a value containing newlines/spaces/unicode.
- capture the EXACT usage/help/error text and which stream it goes to, and the exit codes.
- note that the harness normalises the program name, so record where the program name appears.
Write the exact texts into your report, with escapes, so they can be reproduced character for
character.


HARD CONSTRAINTS for any code you write under /output (the graded deliverable):
- Pure JavaScript for Node.js 18, ES Modules ONLY. Use 'import'/'export'. NEVER 'require' or 'module.exports'.
- Every file under /output MUST use the .mjs extension, and every import MUST include the full
  './name.mjs' suffix.
- ZERO external dependencies. Only local relative imports are allowed. No npm packages. Importing
  node: builtins is permitted but should be unnecessary except possibly nothing at all.
- NO REGULAR EXPRESSIONS ANYWHERE. No regex literals, no 'new RegExp', no String.prototype
  match/matchAll/replace/replaceAll/search/split with a pattern. The tokenizer MUST be a
  hand-written character-by-character lexer.
- Additionally, do not lean on high-level String scanning helpers for the lexing logic
  (indexOf, includes, startsWith, endsWith, lastIndexOf, split, trim, toUpperCase, toLowerCase,
  normalize, localeCompare). Convert the input once with Array.from(text) into an array of
  code-point strings and drive the lexer off array indexing and '===' comparisons, with your own
  ASCII case folding and your own whitespace/strip helpers.
  Permitted primitives: Array.from, array indexing, String.prototype.codePointAt/charCodeAt for
  reading a character's numeric value, String.fromCodePoint/fromCharCode, Array.prototype.join,
  array/number/Map/Set operations.
- No Python. Never invoke 'python'. Never embed or shell out to Python.
- Do not unpack, decompile or read strings out of the executable. This is a strictly black-box
  reimplementation; the ONLY legitimate source of truth is running the executable.

Reference oracle and tooling (read /workspace/spec/FINDINGS.md FIRST — it is confirmed ground truth):
- node /workspace/harness/probe.mjs --inline '["sql a","sql b"]'   -> shows the executable's exact
  stdout/stderr/exit code, JSON-escaped, per input. Entries may also be raw argv arrays, e.g. [["-h"]].
- node /workspace/harness/probe.mjs /path/corpus.json
- node /workspace/harness/compare.mjs /path/corpus.json            -> differential test of
  /output/test2.mjs vs the executable; prints each mismatch; non-zero exit on failure.
- /workspace/corpus/*.json are JSON arrays of test inputs (string => argv ["--a", s]; array => raw argv).
Use probe.mjs/compare.mjs rather than raw shell invocations: it eliminates quoting errors.


Method:
1. Read /workspace/spec/FINDINGS.md first. It is confirmed ground truth — build on it, extend it,
   and challenge anything you can disprove (if you disprove something, say so loudly with evidence).
2. Probe with node /workspace/harness/probe.mjs --inline '[...]' in batches of 10-40 inputs.
   Iterate: form a hypothesis, design an input that DISCRIMINATES between competing hypotheses,
   run it, refine. Do not stop at "it works"; find the boundary of every rule.
3. When a rule is about the splitter's internal counters, use observable probes: append ')' to
   measure the level, and append '; SELECT 1;' to detect whether a split happens.
4. Save every input you probed as a JSON array to /workspace/corpus/probe-cli-argparse.json
   (string entries mean argv ["--a", s]; array entries are raw argv). This becomes a regression
   corpus, so include the interesting cases, not just the boring ones. Aim for 80+ cases.
5. Write a detailed markdown report to /workspace/spec/probe-cli-argparse.md containing: the
   confirmed rules stated in implementable pseudocode, a table of evidence (input -> exact output),
   the hypotheses you eliminated, and any remaining uncertainty.

Precision matters far more than breadth of prose. Every rule you state must be backed by an
input/output pair you actually observed. Return the structured summary.

1	# Established findings — `sqlparse.split()` behaviour (derived black-box from `/workspace/dataset/test2_executable`)
2	
3	These facts are CONFIRMED by running the reference executable. Treat them as ground truth
4	and build on them; do not re-derive them. Anything not listed here is still unknown.
5	
6	## Program shape
7	
8	`main()` parses `--a` (type=str, required) with Python `argparse`, then
9	`print(sqlparse.split(args.a))` — i.e. it prints the **Python `repr` of a list of `str`**.
10	
11	Confirmed CLI behaviour:
12	- `--a VALUE` and `--a=VALUE` both work.
13	- Missing `--a` → usage line + error on **stderr**, exit code **2**.
14	- `-h` / `--help` → help text on stdout, exit code 0. Help text is:
15	  ```
16	  usage: test2_executable [-h] --a A
17	
18	  options:
19	    -h, --help  show this help message and exit
20	    --a A
21	  ```
22	  (the harness normalises the program name, so emit your own program name)
23	- Empty input `--a ""` → prints `[]`.
24	
25	## Output formatting
26	
27	Python list repr: `[` + items joined with `, ` + `]`; `[]` when empty.
28	Each item is a Python string repr: prefer `'...'`; switch to `"..."` only when the string
29	contains `'` **and** does not contain `"`. Escape `\\`, the chosen quote, and control
30	characters (`\n`, `\r`, `\t`, `\xNN`, `\uXXXX`, `\UXXXXXXXX`) exactly as CPython does.
31	
32	## Splitting model (the important part)
33	
34	`split()` returns `[str(stmt).strip() for stmt in statements]`, where statements come from a
35	token-stream splitter. Trailing statements that consist **only of whitespace** are dropped
36	(`--a "   "` → `[]`), but a statement that strips to `''` is otherwise never produced.
37	
38	Splitter state: `level` (paren-ish nesting), `beginDepth`, `inCase`, `inDeclare`, `isCreate`,
39	`consumeWs`, plus the accumulating token list.
40	
41	Per token, in order:
42	1. If `consumeWs` is set and the token is **not** whitespace-proper and **not** a
43	   single-line comment → **emit** the accumulated statement and reset all state.
44	   IMPORTANT: a *newline* token does NOT count as whitespace here (sqlparse lexes
45	   `\r\n` / `\r` / `\n` as a distinct `Newline` token type), so a newline after `;`
46	   terminates the statement, while spaces/tabs do not.
47	   A single-line comment (`--…` / `# …`, including its trailing newline) IS absorbed,
48	   so `SELECT 1; -- t\nSELECT 2` → `['SELECT 1; -- t', 'SELECT 2']`.
49	   A multi-line comment `/*…*/` is NOT absorbed → it starts the next statement.
50	2. `level += changeSplitLevel(tokenType, value)`:
51	   - Punctuation `(` → `+1`, `)` → `-1`
52	   - Non-keyword tokens → `0`
53	   - `unified = value.toUpperCase()`:
54	     - `DECLARE` when `isCreate && beginDepth === 0` → `inDeclare = true`, `+1`
55	     - `BEGIN` → `beginDepth += 1`; returns `+1` when `isCreate`, else `0`
56	     - `END` → if `!inCase` then `beginDepth = max(0, beginDepth - 1)`, else `inCase = false`; returns `-1`
57	     - `IF` / `FOR` / `WHILE` / `CASE` when `isCreate && beginDepth > 0` → (`CASE` sets `inCase = true`) `+1`
58	     - `END IF` / `END FOR` / `END WHILE` → `-1`
59	     - `CREATE` / `CREATE OR REPLACE` → `isCreate = true`, `0`
60	     - otherwise `0`
61	3. Append the token to the current statement.
62	4. If the token is `;` **and** `level <= 0` **and** `beginDepth === 0` → set `consumeWs`.
63	   (The `beginDepth === 0` requirement is confirmed: `BEGIN x )); SELECT 1;` is a single
64	   statement even though `level` is negative there.)
65	5. `GO` (see below) splits **unconditionally** — regardless of `level` and `beginDepth`.
66	
67	At end of input, emit the accumulated statement unless it is whitespace-only.
68	
69	### The BEGIN pre-scan rule (confirmed, unusual)
70	
71	A `BEGIN` keyword only opens a block (only bumps `beginDepth`) when the next token after it
72	— **skipping whitespace, newlines AND comments of both kinds** — is not `;`.
73	
74	Confirmed: `BEGIN;`, `BEGIN ;`, `BEGIN\t;`, `BEGIN /*c*/;`, `BEGIN --c\n;` all split at that
75	`;`, whereas `BEGIN x;`, `BEGIN 1;`, `BEGIN 'x';`, `BEGIN _x;`, `BEGIN foo;`, `BEGIN\nSELECT 1;`
76	and `BEGIN -- c\nSELECT 1;` do not. `SELECT 1 BEGIN; SELECT 2;` also splits, so the rule is
77	positional-independent (it is about what follows `BEGIN`, not about the statement content).
78	
79	### Multi-word keyword tokens (confirmed)
80	
81	The lexer emits some multi-word forms as a SINGLE keyword token, which changes `unified` and
82	therefore the level logic:
83	- `BEGIN TRANSACTION`, `BEGIN WORK`, `BEGIN DEFERRED TRANSACTION`, `BEGIN IMMEDIATE`
84	  → single token, so `unified !== 'BEGIN'` → no block opened → the following `;` splits.
85	  But `BEGIN ATOMIC` is NOT such a form: `BEGIN ATOMIC SELECT 1; SELECT 2;` is one statement.
86	  (The exact accepted word set still needs probing.)
87	- `END IF` is a single token: `CREATE PROCEDURE p AS BEGIN IF x THEN NULL; END IF; END; SELECT 1`
88	  → `['CREATE … END IF; END;', 'SELECT 1']`.
89	- `END CASE` is NOT a single token (`END` + `CASE` separately) — confirmed via
90	  `CREATE PROCEDURE p AS BEGIN CASE WHEN x THEN NULL; END CASE; END; SELECT 1` being ONE statement.
91	- `CREATE OR REPLACE` is a single token and still sets `isCreate`.
92	
93	### Keyword vs. name (confirmed)
94	
95	- An identifier immediately followed by `(` is lexed as a **Name**, not a keyword:
96	  `BEGIN(SELECT 1); SELECT 2;` splits, because `BEGIN` became a Name.
97	- An identifier immediately **after a `.`** is a Name: `SELECT t.begin; SELECT 2` splits.
98	- A quoted identifier is never a keyword: `SELECT "BEGIN"; SELECT 2` splits.
99	- Plain `SELECT begin, 1; SELECT 2` → one statement (lowercase `begin` IS the keyword;
100	  matching is case-insensitive).
101	
102	### `GO` splitter (confirmed)
103	
104	- Case-**sensitive**: `GO` splits; `go`, `gO`, `Go` do not. `GO2` / `GOTO` do not.
105	- `GO 2` is a single token and stays with the preceding statement:
106	  `SELECT 1\nGO 2\nSELECT 2` → `['SELECT 1\nGO 2', 'SELECT 2']`.
107	- It splits at any nesting: `SELECT (1 GO 2)` → `['SELECT (1 GO 2', ')']`,
108	  `BEGIN GO SELECT 1;` → `['BEGIN GO', 'SELECT 1;']`.
109	- After `GO`, the same `consumeWs` absorption applies.
110	
111	### Strings / comments / quoting (confirmed)
112	
113	- `'…'` with `''` doubling **and** backslash escapes: `SELECT 'a\'; b'; SELECT 2` keeps the
114	  `;` inside the literal, but `SELECT 'esc\'; SELECT 2` ends the literal at that quote
115	  (i.e. regex-style backtracking: prefer the escape, fall back to closing the literal so the
116	  literal can terminate).
117	- `"…"` behaves the same way (`""` doubling + backslash escapes).
118	- Backtick `` `…` `` quoting works.
119	- `[…]` bracket quoting works, but only when `[` is NOT preceded by a word character or `]`:
120	  `SELECT [a;b];` keeps the `;`, `SELECT a[1;2];` does not.
121	- Dollar quoting: `$$…$$` and `$tag$…$tag$` hide `;`.
122	- Prefixed literals `E'…'`, `N'…'`, `U&'…'`, `X'0;1'` all hide `;` (the prefix is a separate
123	  token; the quoted part still lexes as a string).
124	- Single-line comments: `--…` needs no space; `#` requires a **following space** —
125	  `SELECT 1 #cmt; still` splits at the `;` (so `#cmt` is not a comment), while
126	  `SELECT 1 # cmt; still` does not.
127	- Unterminated `'…` and `/*…` swallow the rest of the input (no split).
128

135	- `node /workspace/harness/compare.mjs /path/corpus.json` — differential test of

138
